plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control skin: limma DE on TPM + pathway/TF analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon-derived, no raw counts or quantification directories) for 6 lesional vs 6 control skin samples, unpaired, single batch. Per the grounded procedure for TPM/FPKM input (R-0004, R-0072, R-0073), raw-count models (DESeq2/edgeR/voom) are inapplicable and forbidden by the knowledge check; the analysis proceeds on log2(TPM+1) values with limma (trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE eBayes), which is the consensus method for abundance-scale data. Track 1 runs QC on log-transformed abundances (PCA/MDS, sample distances, detected-gene counts) to confirm the two groups separate and no sample is an outlier before fitting any model, then filters low-abundance genes (>=1 TPM in >=6 samples, the smaller group size), fits the limma model with an explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (lesional - control), and selects DE genes by BH-adjusted p-value (not raw p or fold-change alone). Track 2 takes the full ranked gene list (moderated t-statistic, used as the Wald-statistic analog per the knowledge check's permitted method) into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark, then WikiPathways human and GO Biological Process as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store, with the standard 15-500 gene set size window and redundancy collapsing. Track 3 infers transcription factor activity from the same contrast statistic using decoupleR's ulm model on the CollecTRI human regulon network (present in the reference store), which is the correct substitute given ARACNe/VIPER are absent and the cohort (n=6/6) is far too small for a data-driven regulatory network (R-0121). A final report step compiles the DE table, enrichment results with leading-edge genes, TF activity results, and full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, collection versions). No count-based normalization, no batch correction (single batch, none declared), and no cell-composition-based covariate adjustment are applied, since none of those apply to this design; a caveat step in the report notes that a bulk skin sample's cell composition (keratinocyte vs immune infiltrate shifts, well documented in psoriasis) is not decomposed here and any single gene's DE status could partly reflect cell-composition change rather than a cell-intrinsic expression change, which is not testable in more depth on n=6/6 without a dedicated deconvolution step.
